screen1-a1.where: Top-left corner, round white button with two horizontal lines, the lower one shorter.
screen1-a1.expectation: Opens a side menu with the app's sections and my past chats.
screen1-a1.cue: The stacked lines, which is the usual menu picture, in the usual top-left place.

first_pass.why: It is the standard menu glyph and it sits in the same corner on every main screen.

screen1-a2.where: Top left, next to the menu button: light blue pill with a four-point sparkle and the words 'Get Plus'.
screen1-a2.expectation: Opens a page to buy a paid plan.
screen1-a2.cue: The words 'Get Plus'. I know from outside the app that Plus is a paid tier, but the button does not say that.

first_pass.why: 'Get Plus' does not say what Plus is, that it costs money, or that it is a subscription. The sparkle adds nothing literal.
first_pass.solution: Say it literally, e.g. 'Upgrade to paid plan (Plus)'.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing 'Get Plus' shows what Plus is before anything is bought
test_cases.action: Pressed the blue 'Get Plus' pill, looked, pressed the back arrow. Did not press Upgrade or Restore.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: pressing it surprises you, or you could only find out what it was for by trying it, or you still can't tell
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what happens matches what you expected from what you saw, and you would now say it was plain before you pressed it
test_cases.what_happened: A full page opened titled 'ChatGPT Plus' with a Free-versus-Plus feature table, 'Upgrade for $19.99' and 'Renews monthly. Cancel anytime.' Nothing was bought by the first press. The back arrow returned me to the chat screen.

screen1-a2.closing_comment: Pressing it is safe: it shows an information page with the price before anything is bought. But the pill itself still does not say it is a paid plan; I only learned that by pressing.

screen1-a3.where: Top-right corner, round button with an outline that looks like a speech bubble drawn as a broken circle.
screen1-a3.expectation: Either starts a new chat or refreshes something. I cannot decide which.
screen1-a3.cue: Only the picture. The open circle looks like a refresh arrow and like a speech bubble at the same time.

first_pass.why: There is no text and the glyph resembles two different conventions that mean different things.
first_pass.solution: Put a word next to it, e.g. 'Temporary chat' or 'New chat', whichever it actually is.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the round speech-bubble picture at the top right tells you what it is for
test_cases.action: Pressed the broken-circle bubble at the top right, looked, pressed it again.
test_cases.problem_is_real_if: pressing it surprises you, or you could only find out what it was for by trying it, or you still can't tell
test_cases.problem_is_not_real_if: what happens matches what you expected from what you saw, and you would now say it was plain before you pressed it
test_cases.what_happened: The screen changed to 'Temporary chat - This chat won't appear in history. Learn more', the text box said 'Temporary chat', and the icon got a tick. Pressing again turned it off and the text box went back to 'Ask ChatGPT'. While switching off, the word under the heading briefly flipped from 'Personalized' to 'Unpersonalized' before disappearing.

screen1-a3.closing_comment: It is neither new chat nor refresh: it is a temporary-chat switch. Once pressed the screen explains it plainly and it is easy to undo, but I could only find that out by pressing, so the icon still needs a word.

screen1-a4.where: Row in a list above the message bar, headphones icon with the words 'Start a voice chat'.
screen1-a4.expectation: Starts a spoken conversation with the chatbot.

first_pass.why: The text says exactly what it does.

screen1-a5.where: Row in the same list, picture-frame icon with 'Create an image or sticker'.
screen1-a5.expectation: Switches to making an image or a sticker.

first_pass.why: Literal text; it says what I get.

screen1-a6.where: Third row in the list, pencil icon with 'Write or edit'.
screen1-a6.expectation: Opens writing help, like options for editing text.

first_pass.why: It is literal enough. I expect it opens writing options rather than doing anything by itself.

first_pass.solution: Label it 'Attach' or 'Add file or photo', or show the text on first use.

test_cases.targets: whether pressing the plus sign shows what it is for
test_cases.action: Pressed the plus at the bottom left, looked at the list, closed it. Did not choose Camera, Photos or Files.

screen1-a10.where: Bottom-right corner, solid blue circle with white vertical sound-wave bars.
screen1-a10.expectation: Starts some kind of voice mode where it talks back. I am not sure how it differs from the microphone next to it.

first_pass.solution: Label it 'Voice conversation' or similar, so it is distinct from the dictation microphone.
